questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The scientific names of animals are given according to the principles and criteria laid down in the:

solution.explanation: Names of plants follow the International Code for Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN). Animal taxonomists have evolved the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN), which ensures that each animal has a distinct name recognised the world over.
solution.why_others_wrong: ICBN applies to plants, not animals. The five kingdom and two kingdom systems are schemes of classification, not codes for naming.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option B: International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In taxonomy, each category, referred to as a unit of classification, represents a rank and is commonly termed a:

solution.explanation: Classification involves a hierarchy of steps in which each step represents a rank or category. Each category, referred to as a unit of classification, represents a rank and is commonly termed a taxon (plural: taxa).
steps: Unit of classification representing a rank = taxon
solution.why_others_wrong: The specific epithet is the second word of a scientific name. A binomial is the two-word name itself. A phylum is only one particular category, not the general term for every category.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic Categories
solution.final_answer: Option D: taxon

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following plant diseases is named by NCERT as a disease caused by bacteria?

solution.explanation: Some bacteria are pathogens of human beings, crops, farm animals and pets. Cholera, typhoid, tetanus and citrus canker are well-known diseases caused by different bacteria.
solution.why_others_wrong: Wheat rust is caused by the fungus Puccinia. White rust of mustard is caused by the fungus Albugo. Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by a viroid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera (Eubacteria)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Citrus canker

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The name 'virus', given to the infectious agents that pass through bacteria-proof filters, means:

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the name virus, which means venom or poisonous fluid, was given to these agents.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Infectious living fluid' is Beijerinek's term 'Contagium vivum fluidum', not the meaning of 'virus'. Viruses are not cells. Crystals of virus are largely protein, but that is not what the name means.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option C: venom or poisonous fluid

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:

Statement I: The parasitic flagellated protozoan Trypanosoma causes sleeping sickness.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Flagellated protozoans are free-living or parasitic; the parasitic forms cause diseases such as sleeping sickness, e.g., Trypanosoma. Amoeboid protozoans live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil and move by pseudopodia; marine forms have silica shells on their surface.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (kingdom) with List-II (mode of nutrition).

List-I:
A. Monera
B. Fungi
C. Plantae
D. Animalia

List-II:
I. Heterotrophic (holozoic, saprophytic, etc.)
II. Autotrophic (photosynthetic)
III. Heterotrophic (saprophytic or parasitic)
IV. Autotrophic (chemosynthetic and photosynthetic) and heterotrophic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Whittaker's table of the five kingdoms gives the mode of nutrition of Monera as autotrophic (chemosynthetic and photosynthetic) and heterotrophic; of Fungi as heterotrophic (saprophytic or parasitic); of Plantae as autotrophic (photosynthetic); and of Animalia as heterotrophic (holozoic, saprophytic, etc.).
solution.why_others_wrong: Plants are photosynthetic, not chemosynthetic. Fungi absorb food (saprophytic or parasitic) rather than ingest it (holozoic). Only Monera includes chemosynthetic autotrophs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction (Table 2.1: Characteristics of the Five Kingdoms)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.
Statement II: In unicellular organisms such as bacteria and Amoeba, growth and reproduction are clearly separate, mutually exclusive events.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In the majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events. In unicellular organisms such as bacteria, unicellular algae or Amoeba, reproduction is synonymous with growth, i.e., increase in the number of cells, so the two terms are not clearly separable.
steps: Statement II: false, in unicellular organisms reproduction is synonymous with growth
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (characteristics of living organisms)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In phycomycetes, asexual reproduction may take place by non-motile spores produced endogenously in a sporangium. These spores are called:

solution.explanation: In phycomycetes, asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores (motile) or by aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are produced endogenously in a sporangium.
solution.why_others_wrong: Zoospores are the motile spores. Conidia are asexual spores produced exogenously on conidiophores (ascomycetes, deuteromycetes). Ascospores are the sexual spores of ascomycetes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Phycomycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option B: aplanospores

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the NCERT table of organisms with their taxonomic categories, man (Homo sapiens) and the housefly (Musca domestica) are placed together in the same:

solution.explanation: Man: family Hominidae, order Primata, class Mammalia, phylum Chordata. Housefly: family Muscidae, order Diptera, class Insecta, phylum Arthropoda. The two share only the kingdom, Animalia.
solution.why_others_wrong: Chordata and Primata hold man but not the housefly. Insecta holds the housefly but not man.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic Categories (Table 1.1)
solution.final_answer: Option D: kingdom Animalia

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Acellular organisms such as viruses and viroids find no mention in Whittaker's five kingdom classification.
Reason (R): Whittaker's kingdoms are defined using characters such as cell structure, body organisation and mode of nutrition, which acellular particles do not possess.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT notes that the five kingdom classification does not mention lichens and some acellular organisms such as viruses, viroids and prions. Viruses did not find a place in classification because they are not considered truly 'living' if we understand living as having a cell structure. R gives the reason for A.
steps: Lack of cell structure → no place in the classification → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs are commonly known forms of:

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the commonly known forms of basidiomycetes are mushrooms, bracket fungi or puffballs. They grow in soil, on logs and tree stumps, and in living plant bodies as parasites (rusts and smuts).
solution.why_others_wrong: Ascomycetes include yeast, Penicillium, Aspergillus, Claviceps, Neurospora, morels and truffles. Phycomycetes include Mucor, Rhizopus and Albugo. Deuteromycetes include Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Basidiomycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option B: basidiomycetes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about fungi are correct?

(a) Some ascomycetes are coprophilous, that is, they grow on dung.
(b) In ascomycetes, the asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps.
(c) Claviceps and Aspergillus are members of ascomycetes.
(d) Ustilago, the smut fungus, is a member of phycomycetes.
(e) Trichoderma is a member of deuteromycetes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ascomycetes are saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous (growing on dung); their asci are arranged in fruiting bodies called ascocarps; examples include Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora. Ustilago (smut) is a basidiomycete, as are Agaricus and Puccinia. Trichoderma, with Alternaria and Colletotrichum, is a deuteromycete.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain the false statement. (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about kingdom Protista are correct?

(a) Members of Protista are primarily aquatic.
(b) The kingdom forms a link with the kingdoms dealing with plants, animals and fungi.
(c) Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by a process involving cell fusion and zygote formation.
(d) The pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants.
(e) Protozoans are believed to be primitive relatives of plants.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: All single-celled eukaryotes are placed under Protista. Its members are primarily aquatic, and the kingdom forms a link with plants, animals and fungi. Protists reproduce asexually and sexually by cell fusion and zygote formation. The pigments of euglenoids are identical to those of higher plants. Protozoans are heterotrophs and are believed to be primitive relatives of animals, not plants.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) contain the false statement. (a), (c) and (d) only leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A fungus has a septate, branched mycelium. It reproduces only by asexual spores called conidia, and its sexual stage is not known. Which of the following fungi fits this description?

solution.explanation: Fungi in which only the asexual or vegetative phases are known are placed in deuteromycetes. They reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia, and their mycelium is septate and branched. NCERT examples are Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma.
steps: Only asexual phase known + conidia + septate mycelium → deuteromycete
solution.why_others_wrong: Claviceps is an ascomycete, with a known sexual stage (ascospores). Agaricus is a basidiomycete (basidiospores). Mucor is a phycomycete with an aseptate, coenocytic mycelium.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Deuteromycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Colletotrichum

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): All members of kingdom Monera are heterotrophic.
Reason (R): Bacteria are the sole members of kingdom Monera.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Bacteria are the sole members of kingdom Monera, so R is true. But Monera includes autotrophs as well: cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs and some bacteria are chemosynthetic autotrophs. Table 2.1 gives the nutrition of Monera as autotrophic (chemosynthetic and photosynthetic) and heterotrophic. So A is false.
steps: A: false (cyanobacteria and chemosynthetic bacteria are autotrophs)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Kingdom Plantae includes all eukaryotic, chlorophyll-containing organisms, a few of which are partially heterotrophic, such as insectivorous plants and parasites.
Statement II: Bladderwort and Venus fly trap are, like Cuscuta, parasitic plants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Kingdom Plantae includes all eukaryotic chlorophyll-containing organisms commonly called plants. A few members are partially heterotrophic: bladderwort and Venus fly trap are insectivorous plants, while Cuscuta is a parasite.
steps: Statement II: false, bladderwort and Venus fly trap are insectivorous
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Plantae

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Besides water, algae occur in other habitats, and some occur in association with fungi or animals. NCERT gives which of the following as an example of algae growing in association with an animal?

options.text: Algae in the coralloid roots of Cycas
Algae in the gut of ruminants
Algae on the roots of Pinus

solution.explanation: Algae are largely aquatic, but they also occur on moist stones, soils and wood. Some occur in association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g., on sloth bear).
steps: Association with animals → on the sloth bear
solution.why_others_wrong: Coralloid roots of Cycas hold N₂-fixing cyanobacteria, and Cycas is not an animal. The gut of ruminants holds methanogens (archaebacteria). Pinus roots have fungal mycorrhiza.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae
solution.final_answer: Option A: Algae on the sloth bear

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Bryophytes, which include mosses and liverworts, are found commonly growing in:

options.text: moist, shaded areas in the hills

solution.explanation: NCERT describes bryophytes as including the various mosses and liverworts that are found commonly growing in moist shaded areas in the hills.
steps: Bryophytes → moist, shaded areas in the hills
solution.why_others_wrong: Bryophytes need water for fertilisation and are not desert or marine plants. Hot springs are a habitat of thermoacidophile archaebacteria.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option C: moist, shaded areas in the hills

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In heterosporous pteridophytes, the megaspores germinate to give rise to:

solution.explanation: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively.
solution.why_others_wrong: Male gametophytes come from microspores. Spores give gametophytes, not sporophytes. Strobili are compact groups of sporophylls on the sporophyte.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: female gametophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In gymnosperms, the cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules (megasporangia) are called:

solution.explanation: Gymnosperms are heterosporous. The strobili bearing microsporophylls and microsporangia are called microsporangiate or male strobili. The cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules or megasporangia are called macrosporangiate or female strobili.
solution.why_others_wrong: Male strobili bear microsporophylls. Gemma cups are receptacles of gemmae on liverwort thalli. Coralloid roots of Cycas hold cyanobacteria.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option D: macrosporangiate or female strobili

questions.question_text:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Fucus
B. Lycopodium

D. Chlamydomonas

List-II:
I. Gymnosperm with a branched stem
II. Unicellular green alga
III. Brown alga

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Fucus is a member of Phaeophyceae (brown algae). Lycopodium, with Selaginella, belongs to Lycopsida. Cedrus, like Pinus, is a gymnosperm with a branched stem (Cycas is unbranched). Chlamydomonas is a unicellular green alga (Chlorophyceae).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The protonema of a moss is a creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous stage.
Statement II: The leafy stage of a moss consists of upright, slender axes bearing leaves arranged in two rows.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The first stage of the moss gametophyte, the protonema, develops directly from a spore and is a creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous stage. The leafy stage consists of upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves. (Leaf-like appendages in two rows are found in leafy liverworts.)
steps: Statement II: false, the leaves of the moss leafy stage are spirally arranged
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (Mosses)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Members of Phaeophyceae are only rarely found in fresh water.
Reason (R): In brown algae, the protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT's table of algal classes gives the habitat of Phaeophyceae as fresh water (rare), brackish water and salt water, so A is true. R is also true: the protoplast of brown algae contains, besides plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus. R describes the structure of the cell and says nothing about where the algae live, so it does not explain A.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Phaeophyceae; Table 3.1)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In gymnosperms, the nucellus together with the envelopes that protect it forms a composite structure called:

solution.explanation: The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus. The nucellus is protected by envelopes, and the composite structure is called an ovule. Ovules are borne on megasporophylls, which may be clustered to form female cones.
solution.why_others_wrong: A megasporophyll is the structure that bears ovules. A female strobilus is a cluster of megasporophylls. An archegonium is a female sex organ borne on the female gametophyte.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: an ovule

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In members of Chlorophyceae, pyrenoids in the chloroplasts contain protein besides starch. In addition, some green algae may store food in the form of:

solution.explanation: Most green algae have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts; pyrenoids contain protein besides starch. Some algae may store food in the form of oil droplets.
steps: Green algae: starch (pyrenoids) and, in some, oil droplets
solution.why_others_wrong: Laminarin and mannitol are stored by brown algae (Phaeophyceae). Floridean starch is stored by red algae (Rhodophyceae).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Chlorophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option A: oil droplets

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about gymnosperms are correct?

(a) The roots are generally tap roots.
(b) The stem is unbranched in Cycas but branched in Pinus and Cedrus.
(c) The sporophylls are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact cones (strobili).
(d) The seeds formed after fertilisation are enclosed within a fruit.
(e) The leaves are always compound.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Gymnosperm roots are generally tap roots. The stem is unbranched (Cycas) or branched (Pinus, Cedrus). The sporophylls are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact cones. The ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, so the seeds are not covered (no fruit forms). The leaves may be simple or compound.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes (d) or (e), which are false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Members of Rhodophyceae reproduce sexually by non-motile gametes.
Statement II: Brown algae range from simple, branched, filamentous forms such as Ectocarpus to profusely branched forms such as kelps.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Red algae reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation, asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes. Brown algae show great variation in size and form, from simple branched filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms represented by kelps.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Phaeophyceae; Rhodophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the pigments and flagella of algae are correct?

(a) Members of Phaeophyceae contain chlorophyll a and c, carotenoids and xanthophylls.
(b) Members of Chlorophyceae have 2–8 equal, apical flagella.

solution.concept: Divisions of algae and their main characteristics

steps: (c) false: chlorophyll b belongs to green algae
(e) false: brown algae have 2 unequal, lateral flagella
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) include a false statement; the remaining combination must contain (a), (b) and (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Table 3.1: Divisions of Algae and their Main Characteristics)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Algae form the basis of the food cycles of all aquatic animals.
Reason (R): Algae are photosynthetic and are primary producers of energy-rich compounds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that algae are of paramount importance as primary producers of energy-rich compounds which form the basis of the food cycles of all aquatic animals. Because they make these compounds by photosynthesis, they stand at the base of aquatic food cycles; R explains A.
steps: Primary producers → base of food cycles → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which feature is shared by bryophytes and pteridophytes but is NOT found in gymnosperms?

options.text: A dominant sporophyte with true roots, stems and leaves
A gametophyte with an independent, free-living existence
Spores produced by meiosis in sporangia

solution.concept: Comparing the gametophytes of the plant groups
solution.explanation: In bryophytes the gametophyte is the main plant body, and in pteridophytes the gametophyte (prothallus) is small, multicellular and free-living. Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence; they remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes.
solution.why_others_wrong: A dominant sporophyte with true organs and vascular tissues is found in pteridophytes and gymnosperms but not in bryophytes. Spores formed by meiosis in sporangia occur in all three groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes; Pteridophytes; Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: A gametophyte with an independent, free-living existence

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In gymnosperms, following fertilisation, the zygote develops into an embryo and the ovules into seeds.
Statement II: In gymnosperms, the ovules are borne on microsporophylls.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Following fertilisation, the zygote develops into an embryo and the ovules into seeds, which are not covered. The ovules are borne on megasporophylls, which may be clustered to form female cones; microsporophylls bear microsporangia.
steps: Statement II: false, ovules are borne on megasporophylls
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly shows the development of the female gametophyte in a gymnosperm?

options.text: Nucellus cell → four megaspores by mitosis → megaspore mother cell → female gametophyte bearing antheridia
Megasporophyll → pollen grain → megaspore mother cell → female gametophyte shed from the ovule
Megaspore mother cell → two megaspores by meiosis → both form free-living female gametophytes
Nucellus cell → megaspore mother cell → four megaspores by meiosis → one megaspore forms a multicellular female gametophyte bearing archegonia

solution.explanation: The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus. It divides meiotically to form four megaspores. One of the megaspores, enclosed within the megasporangium, develops into a multicellular female gametophyte that bears two or more archegonia. The female gametophyte is retained within the megasporangium.
steps: 1 megaspore → female gametophyte with 2 or more archegonia
solution.why_others_wrong: The megaspores are formed by meiosis, not mitosis, and the female gametophyte bears archegonia, not antheridia. Pollen grains are male gametophytes and the female gametophyte is retained, not shed. Meiosis gives four megaspores, and gymnosperm gametophytes are not free-living.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option D: Nucellus cell → megaspore mother cell → four megaspores by meiosis → one megaspore forms a multicellular female gametophyte bearing archegonia

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In plants such as grass, Monstera and the banyan tree, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle. Such roots are called:

solution.explanation: In some plants, like grass, Monstera and the banyan tree, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle and are called adventitious roots.
steps: Roots not from the radicle → adventitious
solution.why_others_wrong: A tap root is the direct elongation of the radicle, and lateral roots are its branches. Root hairs are unicellular outgrowths of the epidermis, not roots.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root
solution.final_answer: Option D: adventitious roots

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In which of the following plants does a slender lateral branch arise from the base of the main axis, grow aerially for some time and then arch downwards to touch the ground?

solution.explanation: In plants like mint and jasmine, a slender lateral branch arises from the base of the main axis and, after growing aerially for some time, arches downwards to touch the ground.
steps: Mint and jasmine → lateral branch arching down to the ground
solution.why_others_wrong: In Pistia, a lateral branch with short internodes bears a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots at each node. Opuntia has a flattened green photosynthetic stem. Ginger has an underground stem that stores food.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Stem (Modifications of Stem)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Mint

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The fleshy leaves of onion and garlic store food.
Statement II: Leaves originate from the shoot apical meristem and are arranged in an acropetal order.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Leaves are often modified; the fleshy leaves of onion and garlic store food. A leaf is a lateral, generally flattened structure borne on the stem; leaves originate from shoot apical meristems and are arranged in an acropetal order.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The sepals of a flower are green and leaf-like. Their main function is to:

options.text: protect the flower in the bud stage

solution.explanation: The calyx is the outermost whorl of the flower and its members are called sepals. Generally, sepals are green, leaf-like and protect the flower in the bud stage.
steps: Sepals → protection in the bud stage
solution.why_others_wrong: Attracting insects is the role of the usually brightly coloured corolla. Pollen grains are produced in the anthers. The fruit wall develops from the ovary wall.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Parts of a Flower (Calyx)
solution.final_answer: Option C: protect the flower in the bud stage

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The corolla of a flower is usually brightly coloured.
Reason (R): Bright colours of the corolla attract insects for pollination.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The corolla is composed of petals, which are usually brightly coloured to attract insects for pollination. R gives the purpose that the bright colour serves.
steps: Colour attracts pollinating insects → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Parts of a Flower (Corolla)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Stamens united into two bundles, as in pea, are described as diadelphous.
Statement II: In mustard and tomato, the carpels of the gynoecium are free, so the gynoecium is apocarpous.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Stamens may be united into one bundle (monoadelphous, china rose), two bundles (diadelphous, pea) or more than two bundles (polyadelphous, citrus). Carpels are free (apocarpous) in lotus and rose, but fused (syncarpous) in mustard and tomato.
steps: Statement II: false, mustard and tomato are syncarpous
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Parts of a Flower (Androecium; Gynoecium)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (type of placentation) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Marginal
B. Parietal
C. Free central
D. Basal

List-II:
I. Placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it
II. Ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent
III. Ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on its peripheral part
IV. Placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture and the ovules form two rows on it

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Marginal: the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on it in two rows (pea). Parietal: ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on its peripheral part (mustard, Argemone). Free central: ovules on a central axis, septa absent (Dianthus, Primrose). Basal: placenta at the base of the ovary with a single ovule (sunflower, marigold).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap parietal with free central (ovules on the ovary wall versus on a central axis) or marginal with basal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Parts of a Flower (Gynoecium: placentation)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Mango and coconut fruits are drupes. Drupes develop from:

options.text: bicarpellary superior ovaries and are many-seeded
monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one-seeded
monocarpellary inferior ovaries and are one-seeded
multicarpellary superior ovaries and are one-seeded

solution.explanation: In mango and coconut, the fruit is known as a drupe. Drupes develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one-seeded.
steps: Drupe: monocarpellary + superior ovary + one seed
solution.why_others_wrong: Each wrong option changes one of the three features NCERT gives: the number of carpels, the position of the ovary or the number of seeds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Fruit
solution.final_answer: Option B: monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one-seeded

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Gram, arhar, sem and moong are members of the family Fabaceae that are important as sources of:

solution.explanation: Many plants of Fabaceae are sources of pulses (gram, arhar, sem, moong, soyabean); edible oil (soyabean, groundnut); dye (Indigofera); fibres (sunhemp); fodder (Sesbania, Trifolium); ornamentals (lupin, sweet pea); and medicine (muliathi).
solution.why_others_wrong: Edible oil comes from soyabean and groundnut, fibre from sunhemp, and fodder from Sesbania and Trifolium.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Fabaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option B: pulses

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a maize grain, the embryo is small and is situated:

options.text: at the centre of the endosperm, surrounded by it on all sides
in a groove at one end of the endosperm

solution.explanation: In cereals such as maize, the endosperm is bulky and stores food. The embryo is small and situated in a groove at one end of the endosperm. It has one large, shield-shaped cotyledon (scutellum) and a short axis with a plumule and a radicle.
steps: Maize embryo: small, in a groove at one end of the endosperm
solution.why_others_wrong: The embryo is not embedded at the centre, and it lies inside the grain, not outside the fruit wall. Two fleshy cotyledons are found in dicotyledonous seeds; maize has a single cotyledon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Seed (Structure of a Monocotyledonous Seed)
solution.final_answer: Option D: in a groove at one end of the endosperm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:

Statement I: Underground stems of some plants, such as grass and strawberry, spread to new niches, and when the older parts die new plants are formed.
Statement II: In Eichhornia, a lateral branch with short internodes bears at each node a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Underground stems of grass and strawberry spread to new niches, and new plants form when older parts die. A lateral branch with short internodes, each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots, is found in aquatic plants like Pistia and Eichhornia.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Stem (Modifications of Stem)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The corolla may be tubular, bell-shaped, funnel-shaped or wheel-shaped.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The shape and colour of the corolla vary greatly; it may be tubular, bell-shaped, funnel-shaped or wheel-shaped. Each carpel has a stigma, style and ovary; the stigma is usually at the tip of the style and is the receptive surface for pollen grains. The ovary is the enlarged basal part.
steps: Statement II: false, the stigma is at the tip of the style
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Parts of a Flower (Corolla; Gynoecium)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the family Liliaceae are correct?

(a) The inflorescence is solitary or cymose, often in umbellate clusters.
(b) The perianth has six tepals (3 + 3), often united into a tube, with valvate aestivation.
(c) The androecium has six stamens, arranged as 3 + 3.
(d) The ovary is trilocular, with many ovules on axile placentation.
(e) The fruit is a legume.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Liliaceae ('lily family') is a characteristic monocot family. Inflorescence solitary/cymose, often umbellate clusters. Perianth: tepals six (3+3), often united into a tube, valvate aestivation. Androecium: stamens six, 3+3. Gynoecium: tricarpellary, syncarpous, superior ovary, trilocular with many ovules, axile placentation. Fruit: capsule, rarely berry. A legume is the fruit of Fabaceae.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) contain the false statement. (b), (c) and (d) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Liliaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A flower has its stamens united into a single bundle and a multilocular ovary in which the ovules are attached to an axial placenta. Among the following, this description fits the flower of:

solution.explanation: China rose has monoadelphous stamens (united into one bundle) and axile placentation (placenta axial, ovules attached to it in a multilocular ovary).
steps: One bundle of stamens → monoadelphous → china rose
Axial placenta in a multilocular ovary → axile → china rose, tomato, lemon
solution.why_others_wrong: Pea has diadelphous stamens and marginal placentation. Mustard has parietal placentation. Dianthus has free central placentation in an ovary without septa.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Parts of a Flower (Androecium; Gynoecium)
solution.final_answer: Option A: china rose

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the families Fabaceae and Solanaceae are correct?

(a) In Fabaceae, the calyx has five sepals and is gamosepalous.
(b) In Fabaceae, the androecium has ten stamens, which are diadelphous, and the anthers are dithecous.
(c) Solanaceae is widely distributed in the tropics, the subtropics and even the temperate zones.
(d) In Fabaceae, the ovary is inferior.
(e) In Solanaceae, the inflorescence is solitary, axillary or cymose, as in Solanum.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Solanaceae ('potato family') is widely distributed in tropics, subtropics and even temperate zones; its inflorescence is solitary, axillary or cymose as in Solanum.
steps: (d) false: the ovary of Fabaceae is superior
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain the false statement. (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Fabaceae; Solanaceae)

questions.subject: Botany

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Besides the pulp of fruits such as guava, pear and sapota, sclereids are commonly found in:

options.text: the companion cells of the phloem
the fruit walls of nuts, the seed coats of legumes and the leaves of tea

solution.explanation: Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities. They are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts; the pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota; the seed coats of legumes; and the leaves of tea.
steps: Sclereids: fruit walls of nuts, pulp of guava/pear/sapota, seed coats of legumes, tea leaves
solution.why_others_wrong: Root hairs, guard cells and companion cells are living cells; sclereids are dead, highly thickened cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Sclerenchyma)
solution.final_answer: Option D: the fruit walls of nuts, the seed coats of legumes and the leaves of tea

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The stomatal aperture, the guard cells and the surrounding subsidiary cells are together called the:

solution.explanation: Stomata are structures in the epidermis of leaves. Each stoma has two guard cells enclosing the stomatal pore; a few specialised epidermal cells near the guard cells are subsidiary cells. The stomatal aperture, guard cells and surrounding subsidiary cells together are called the stomatal apparatus.
steps: Aperture + guard cells + subsidiary cells = stomatal apparatus
solution.why_others_wrong: Epidermal appendages are trichomes and hairs. The stele is all the tissue inside the endodermis. Bulliform cells are large empty cells in the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (Epidermal Tissue System)
solution.final_answer: Option D: stomatal apparatus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Cells formed by the divisions of primary and secondary meristems become structurally and functionally specialised and lose the ability to divide. Such cells constitute the:

solution.explanation: Following divisions of cells in both primary and secondary meristems, the newly formed cells become structurally and functionally specialised and lose the ability to divide. Such cells are termed permanent or mature cells and constitute the permanent tissues.
steps: Specialised cells that no longer divide → permanent tissues
solution.why_others_wrong: Intercalary, lateral and apical meristems are all meristematic tissues, whose cells keep the ability to divide.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option B: permanent tissues

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Permanent tissues having all cells similar in structure and function are called simple tissues.
Statement II: In flowering plants, xylem fibres are the main water-transporting elements.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Permanent tissues having all cells similar in structure and function are called simple tissues; those with many different types of cells are complex tissues. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water-transporting elements. Xylem fibres have highly thickened walls and obliterated central lumens.
steps: Statement II: false, tracheids and vessels are the main water-transporting elements
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent Tissues; Xylem)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The sieve tube elements and companion cells are connected by pit fields present between their common longitudinal walls.
Statement II: Phloem parenchyma is made up of elongated, tapering, cylindrical cells that have dense cytoplasm and a nucleus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Companion cells are specialised parenchymatous cells closely associated with sieve tube elements; the two are connected by pit fields present between their common longitudinal walls. Phloem parenchyma is made up of elongated, tapering cylindrical cells which have dense cytoplasm and a nucleus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following belong to the ground tissue system of primary stems and roots?

(a) Cortex
(b) Pericycle
(c) Pith
(d) Phloem
(e) Epidermis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: All tissues except the epidermis and the vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. Parenchymatous cells of the ground tissue are usually present in the cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays in primary stems and roots. Phloem belongs to the vascular tissue system and the epidermis to the epidermal tissue system.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) include a tissue of another tissue system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (The Ground Tissue System)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (meristem) with List-II (position).

List-I:
A. Root apical meristem
B. Shoot apical meristem
C. Intercalary meristem
D. Lateral meristem

List-II:
I. Cylindrical meristem in the mature regions of roots and shoots, lateral in position
II. Between mature tissues, as in grasses
III. Distant-most region of the stem axis
IV. Tip of the root

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The root apical meristem occupies the tip of a root, while the shoot apical meristem occupies the distant-most region of the stem axis. Intercalary meristems occur between mature tissues, as in grasses. Lateral meristems appear later, in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, particularly those that produce woody axes, and are lateral and cylindrical.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange the two apical meristems, or the intercalary and lateral meristems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Meristematic Tissues)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Xylem and phloem are described as complex tissues.
Reason (R): Each is made up of more than one type of cell, and these cells work together as a unit.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cells that work together as a unit. Xylem (tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma) and phloem (sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, phloem fibres) are the complex tissues in plants. questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The cortex of a dicot stem consists of three sub-zones. Which of the following gives them in the correct order from outside inwards?

solution.explanation: The outer hypodermis has a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis. Below it are the cortical layers of rounded, thin-walled parenchyma with conspicuous intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis (starch sheath). The pericycle lies inside the endodermis and is not part of the cortex.
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option is the reverse order. The second places the endodermis in the middle, but it is the innermost layer. The third includes the pericycle, which lies inside the endodermis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Dicotyledonous Stem)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Hypodermis, cortical layers, endodermis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about xylem are correct?

(a) Tracheids are dead and without protoplasm; the inner layers of their walls have thickenings that vary in form.
(b) Vessel members are devoid of protoplasm.
(c) Xylem conducts water and minerals from the leaves to the stem and roots.
(d) Besides conduction, xylem provides mechanical strength to plant parts.
(e) A vessel member has lignified walls and a large central cavity.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Xylem functions as a conducting tissue for water and minerals from the roots to the stem and leaves, and also provides mechanical strength. Tracheids are elongated, dead cells without protoplasm, with thick lignified walls whose inner layers bear thickenings of various forms. A vessel is a long cylindrical tube of many vessel members, each with lignified walls and a large central cavity; vessel members are devoid of protoplasm.
steps: (c) false: from roots to stem and leaves
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes (c), which reverses the direction of conduction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Xylem)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a dicot root, both the tangential and the radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of a water-impermeable, waxy material in the form of Casparian strips.
Statement II: In a dicot stem, the cortical layers below the hypodermis consist of rounded, thin-walled parenchymatous cells with conspicuous intercellular spaces.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In the dicot root, the tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy suberin as Casparian strips. In the dicot stem, the cortical layers below the hypodermis are rounded, thin-walled parenchymatous cells with conspicuous intercellular spaces.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Dicotyledonous Root; Dicotyledonous Stem)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf, the vascular bundles are all of nearly similar size.
Reason (R): The size of a vascular bundle depends on the size of the vein, and the veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In a dorsiventral leaf, the size of the vascular bundles depends on the size of the veins, and the veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves; so the bundles vary in size and A is false. Vascular bundles of nearly similar size (except the main veins) are a feature of the isobilateral (monocot) leaf with parallel venation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Dorsiventral (Dicot) Leaf)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes collenchyma in relation to the dicot stem?

options.text: It forms semi-lunar patches above the phloem as part of the pericycle
It forms the sclerenchymatous hypodermis found in monocot stems
It occurs in layers below the epidermis, as a homogeneous layer or in patches, and the collenchymatous hypodermis gives mechanical strength to the young stem
It consists of dead cells with lignified walls that lack intercellular spaces

solution.explanation: Collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants, either as a homogeneous layer or in patches. In the dicot stem, the hypodermis consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis, which provide mechanical strength to the young stem.
steps: Collenchyma: below epidermis in dicots, homogeneous layer or patches
Dicot stem hypodermis = collenchyma → strength to young stem
solution.why_others_wrong: The semi-lunar patches of the pericycle are sclerenchyma. The hypodermis of the monocot stem is sclerenchymatous, not collenchymatous. Collenchyma cells are living, with walls thickened at the corners by cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin, not lignin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Collenchyma); Dicotyledonous Stem
solution.final_answer: Option C: It occurs in layers below the epidermis, as a homogeneous layer or in patches, and the collenchymatous hypodermis gives mechanical strength to the young stem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae and:

options.text: mycoplasma and PPLO (pleuro pneumonia like organisms)

solution.explanation: The prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma and PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms).
steps: Prokaryotes: bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma, PPLO
solution.why_others_wrong: Yeast (a fungus), Amoeba, Euglena, Chlamydomonas, diatoms and desmids are all eukaryotes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option C: mycoplasma and PPLO (pleuro pneumonia like organisms)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In both plant and animal cells, the main arena of cellular activities, where various chemical reactions keep the cell in the 'living state', is the:

solution.explanation: The cytoplasm is the main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells. Various chemical reactions occur in it to keep the cell in the 'living state'.
steps: Main arena of cellular activities → cytoplasm
solution.why_others_wrong: The nucleus holds the genetic material, the cell wall gives shape and protection, and the vacuole stores water, sap and materials not useful for the cell.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', An Overview of Cell
solution.final_answer: Option A: cytoplasm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Ribosomes are:

options.text: composed of DNA and proteins, and surrounded by a single membrane
composed of RNA and proteins, and not surrounded by any membrane
composed of lipids and proteins, and surrounded by a double membrane
composed of RNA and lipids, and surrounded by a single membrane

solution.explanation: Ribosomes are granular structures first observed under the electron microscope by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ribosomes contain RNA, not DNA, and are not membrane-bound; every wrong option adds a membrane or a wrong component.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Ribosomes)
solution.final_answer: Option B: composed of RNA and proteins, and not surrounded by any membrane

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures in the cytoplasm, collectively called the cytoskeleton, consists of:

options.text: cristae, matrix and the outer membrane

solution.explanation: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton. It is involved in mechanical support, motility and maintenance of cell shape.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cisternae and vesicles describe the Golgi apparatus and ER, cristae and matrix the mitochondrion, and grana and stroma the chloroplast.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Cytoskeleton)
solution.final_answer: Option D: microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Animal cells have centrioles, which are absent in almost all plant cells.
Statement II: Plant cells possess cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT's comparison of plant and animal cells: plant cells possess cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells; animal cells have centrioles, which are absent in almost all plant cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Normally there is one nucleus per cell. Which of the following are cited by NCERT as mature cells that lack a nucleus?

options.text: Nerve cells and white blood cells
Erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants
Mesophyll cells and root hair cells

solution.explanation: Normally there is only one nucleus per cell, though variations in the number of nuclei are frequently observed. Some mature cells even lack a nucleus, e.g., erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants.
steps: Mature cells without nucleus: mammalian erythrocytes, sieve tube cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Companion cells, guard cells, nerve cells, white blood cells, mesophyll cells and root hair cells all have a nucleus. (The functions of sieve tubes are controlled by the nucleus of the companion cell.)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Nucleus)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Plasmodesmata are pores in the nuclear envelope through which RNA moves into the cytoplasm.
Statement II: The cell wall helps in cell-to-cell interaction and provides a barrier to undesirable macromolecules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The cell wall and middle lamellae may be traversed by plasmodesmata, which connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells; the passages for RNA in the nuclear envelope are nuclear pores. Besides giving shape and protecting the cell from mechanical damage and infection, the cell wall helps in cell-to-cell interaction and provides a barrier to undesirable macromolecules.
steps: Statement I: false, plasmodesmata connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Cell Wall)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of the cell) with List-II (what it contains).

List-I:
A. Mitochondrial matrix
B. Thylakoids
C. Chloroplast stroma
D. Vacuole

List-II:
I. Water, sap, excretory products and other materials not useful for the cell
II. Single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules and 70S ribosomes
III. Enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins
IV. Chlorophyll pigments

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The mitochondrial matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and components for protein synthesis. The chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids. The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins. The vacuole contains water, sap, excretory products and other materials not useful for the cell.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the matrix with the stroma, the thylakoids with the stroma, or the stroma with the vacuole.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Mitochondria; Plastids; Vacuoles)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the number of mitochondria per cell is variable depending on the physiological activity of the cells. R states the cause of the variation in A.
steps: Number depends on activity → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Mitochondria)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the cell membrane are correct?

(a) The lipid component of the membrane mainly consists of phosphoglycerides.
(b) Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by simple diffusion along the concentration gradient.
